Jordan (Acme): hey team — after the 09:00 deploy our docs generator started returning extra backticks inside fenced code blocks. this started affecting prod pages, markdown parser chokes. sending example below. not something we changed on our end. :frowning:

Jordan (Acme): request we send (abbreviated):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-v4","input":"Render docs for foo() with example","max_tokens":400,"stop":["```"]}'
```

Jordan (Acme): response snippet (non-streaming):
```json
{
  "id": "resp_abc123",
  "output": "Here is the example:\n```python\ndef foo():\n    return 42\n```\n```\n\nSome extra text..."
}
```

Jordan (Acme): see the extra standalone ``` after the intended closing fence. sometimes the response also injects an extra leading ``` or duplicates the opening fence. this breaks our pipeline that expects a single fenced block per example.

Sam N - Customer Success: @Jordan sorry about that — we saw a few reports this morning. can you confirm: streaming or non-streaming? model name exactly? any request_id/response headers you can paste? also which region (us-east-1 / eu-west-1)?

Jordan (Acme): non-streaming. model reported in our code: "redwood-instruct-v4". response header x-request-id: resp_abc123. region us-east-1. started ~09:05 UTC after what looked like a canary. this happened to 3 separate requests. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started by marta at 2026-03-15T09:00:12Z for rollout-id rlf_2026_0315_canary (10% traffic).

Sam N - Customer Success: thanks — looping in Priya from the inference team to investigate, assigning here. @Priya R - can you take a look? looks like stop-sequence handling or post-decode formatting bug.

Priya R - Eng (ML): digging in. first guess: stop-seq detection is triggering but the post-processing that strips/normalizes fenced-code markup may be running after we emit a leftover fence. could also be tokenizer change where backticks tokenized differently and we end up with an extra token in the decoded stream. is this only literal backtick fences or other delimiters too?

Jordan (Acme): only seeing it for triple-backtick fences so far. single backticks inline code unaffected. some customers also reported extra trailing "###" for markdown headings but haven't reproduced that.

Priya R - Eng (ML): ok. can you paste the exact stop array you used? also, can you try a quick experiment: repeat the same request but set stop to "\\n```" (i.e. include the leading newline) and see if that avoids the duplicate fence? might be a whitespace edging issue.

Jordan (Acme): tried adding "\\n```" — that reduces duplication but in one run it produced a closing fence plus an extra blank fence line (still broken). attaching full request/response payloads to the support ticket.

Priya R - Eng (ML): thanks. I'm running local repro with the exact model bundle that was pushed in canary. quick tokenization check:
```python
# tokenization snippet (dev env)
from tokenizer import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer('redwood-instruct-v4')
print(t.tokenize('```'))
# output: ['`', '`', '`']
```
looks normal. suspect the regression is in the decoding/post-processing pipeline that merges stop detection with markdown normalization. I'll run the same prompt through the previous commit (pre-rollout) to diff outputs.

Marta - Platform: note — the canary includes a change to the decode pipeline: small refactor to stream termination logic + an unrelated reorder of the markdown-fence sanitizer. rolling forward to 10% started at 09:00. we can pause/rollback if needed.

Priya R - Eng (ML): reproducer success on canary bundle — non-streaming decode sometimes emits an extra fence token when stop boundary aligns with byte-aligned token boundary. probable off-by-one in the fence-trim stage. I have a minimal failing test and a plausible fix (ensure fence-trim runs before any normalization passes and drop empty fence-only outputs).

Sam N - Customer Success: thanks. what's the plan/timeline? customers are seeing site rendering errors. some have automated PRs that now fail CI because docs parser fails lint.

Priya R - Eng (ML): plan:
- immediate: pause canary (rollback to pre-canary) to stop new instances getting the bundle. (Marta)
- short-term (hotfix): patch the fence-trim order, add unit tests for various stop tokens, deploy to canary again. target ~60-90m.
- monitor telemetry for "extra-fence" regression metric and customer repros. will push patch to main and request expedited deploy.

Marta - Platform: pausing canary now. traffic reverted to previous stable bundle at 09:18 UTC. I'll also mark rollout as blocked until patch lands.

Priya R - Eng (ML): patch PR opened: PR #4728 — changes decode order + adds test cases for triple-backtick and leading-newline stops. requesting review from eng runtime. if green, we can re-canary within ~45m.

Sam N - Customer Success: @Jordan putting you on the short list for canary verification — if you're willing we can route a small percent of your traffic to the patched canary for validation.

Jordan (Acme): yes please — would appreciate that. we can watch a handful of requests and confirm. thanks for the quick turnaround.

Priya R - Eng (ML): thanks. additional mitigation: as workaround until canary is validated, prefer stop sequences that include a trailing sentinel (e.g. "\\n```END" then strip END in post) — I know it's hacky but avoids ambiguous fence-only outputs.

Sam N - Customer Success: keeping ticket updated and will post when we start re-canary. @Jordan I will DM to set up verification window.

Jordan (Acme): thx. appreciate the quick action and the workaround tip. :thumbsup:

Priya R - Eng (ML): follow-ups: add regression alert to QA that runs prompt-set against decoding stages; add an end-to-end test for markdown renderers to catch this class of issue earlier.

Marta - Platform: logging incident note and timeline for postmortem. will include which commit introduced reorder. tagging infra to look for any other decode-related refactors this cycle.

Sam N - Customer Success: closing loop for now — will update thread when canary redeploys and when Jordan verifies. if anyone finds additional customers seeing weird fence tokens, add their request_ids to the ticket.

Jordan (Acme): confirmed after canary + patch verification that duplicates are gone. thanks everyone.
